ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a large equilateral triangle subdivided into a triangular grid with side length 6 small-triangle units, making 36 congruent smallest equilateral triangles. The shaded region is one triangle whose vertices lie on grid intersections: the left vertex is on the left side one unit above the base, the upper-right vertex is on the right side at the midpoint grid intersection, and the lower-right vertex is on the base four units from the left base corner. Reasoning: Label the left base corner A=(0,0), the right base corner B=(6,0), and the top C=(0,6) in oblique triangular-lattice coordinates. From the shaded vertices in the image, take P=(0,1), Q=(3,3), and R=(4,0). Then Q-P=(3,2) and R-P=(4,-1). The lattice-area rule gives the shaded triangle's area in units of one small equilateral triangle as |det((3,2),(4,-1))| = |3*(-1) - 2*4| = |-11| = 11. Each small triangle has area 10 cm^2, so K = 11*10 = 110.

Label the left base corner A=(0,0), the right base corner B=(6,0), and the top C=(0,6) using oblique triangular-lattice coordinates. From the shading, the shaded triangle’s vertices are P=(0,1) on the left side, Q=(3,3) on the right side, and R=(4,0) on the base. Use the lattice-area rule: for points expressed in the two 60-degree lattice basis directions, the absolute determinant of two side vectors gives the area in units of one small equilateral triangle. Compute |det(Q-P, R-P)| = |det((3,2),(4,-1))| = 11. Since each small triangle has area 10 cm^2, K=11*10=110.

method.method_draft: First read the image as a side-6 equilateral triangle subdivided into 36 unit small triangles. The shaded triangle connects P on the left side one unit above the base, Q on the right side three units above the base, and R on the base four units from the left. Instead of computing the shaded area directly, subtract the three unshaded corner triangles from the whole large triangle. The top corner triangle has side lengths 5 and 3 along the two slanted sides, so its area is 5*3=15 small triangles. The bottom-left corner triangle has side lengths 1 and 4 along the left side and base, so its area is 1*4=4 small triangles. The bottom-right corner triangle has side lengths 3 and 2 along the right side and base, so its area is 3*2=6 small triangles. Thus the shaded region has 36-(15+4+6)=11 small-triangle areas, so K=11*10=110.
